answer: Agents earn influence as age times honest epochs: a slow trust curve where each correct interaction adds weight, but new accounts start near zero no matter how many are spun up. Identity is verified by a cryptographic mirror of past behavior, signed into an onyx ledger of reputation that cannot be forged or copied, while a quill of attestations from long-lived peers records honest work. An attacker pays the real cost of time and consistent honesty; clones stay weightless, so flooding gains nothing.
